newsitem.title: FINLAND: SWIMMING-WINNING RETURN FOR SIEVINEN AFTER LONG BREAK.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-WINNING RETURN FOR SIEVINEN AFTER LONG BREAK.

text.p: World champion Jani Sievinen made a winning return to international competition after the disappointment of last July's Atlanta Olympics, scoring an individual medley double on the first day of a World Cup swimming meeting on Wednesday.

The Finn took three months off after competing in Atlanta where he felt below his best and had to settle for the silver medal in the 200 metres individual medley, the event he had been expected to win. He had earlier failed to qualify for the 400 individual medley final.

Sievinen, reigning world long-course 200 individual medley champion and world record-holder, won the 100 and 400 individual medley events by vast margins on the first day of the two-day Espoo meeting, third stop in the eight-venue World Cup short-course series.

The Finn, holder of three world short-course records, clocked four minutes 16.43 seconds in the 400, more than 10 seconds outside his world record mark, and 54.98 in the 100, nearly two seconds outside his world time. But in both races he left the opposition way behind.

Sievinen, who won three titles at the 1995 European championships, still hopes to become the first Finn to win an Olympic swimming gold at the 2000 Games in Sydney and signed a personal sponsorship deal in Espoo with four Finnish companies who are supporting his ambition.
"It was difficult to get started again but since December I've been training seriously again. I've still got one more job to do at the Olympics," Sievinen said.
The Espoo event will be Sievinen's only appearance in the World Cup series. He is concentrating his training this year on the European long-course championships in Seville, Spain, in August.

China, with a small team of four men and four women, continued their winning ways with five victories on the first day after successful outings in the two Asian legs of the World Cup circuit in Hong Kong and Beijing.

All four Chinese women were victorious. Mi Tong comfortably won the 100 breaststroke, Guo Wei took the 200 freestyle, Jia Yuanyuan edged out Slovenia's Metka Sparavac by just 0.02 seconds in the 50 backstroke and Chen Yan outclassed the opposition in the 200 individual medley. Ding Chujin was China's lone men's winner, taking the 50 breaststroke in 28.00.
Ukraine's Pavlo Khnykin completed a golden double, winning the men's 100 freestyle in 49.24 and 50 butterfly in 24.40.
